title: Cross-Team Exposure Trellis and Measurement Cheatsheet (draft)
body:
Purpose
This note defines a compact, operational playbook we can use for small-to-medium LLM feature exposures across teams (hosted API, Dedicated, Private). Intended audience: product owners, experiment owners, solutions engineers, SREs, and oncall. This is intentionally terse — a living cheatsheet for run-of-day decisions and handoffs.

Key concept: exposure trellis
- Trellis = staggered exposure grid combining user slice size, traffic weight, and feature surface (inference model variant, prompt tweak, reranking threshold).
- Why trellis: helps reason about orthogonal risk (who sees it, how often, which model path) and choose minimal blast radius for behavioral risk.

Exposure tiers (short labels we use):
- init-run (synthetic + internal): internal QA + synthetic cohort only, 0% prod traffic.
- smoke (alpha): small internal+pilot customers, <0.1% traffic, human-in-loop checks.
- micro (beta): 0.1%–1% traffic, microcohorts (power users, specific geos), automated telemetry.
- ramp (gamma): 1%–10% traffic, controlled slices, daily steward check-ins.
- broad (delta): >10% traffic, full rollout governed by SLA/cost gates.

Roles and brief responsibilities
- Feature Owner (product): hypothesis, rollout schedule, success metrics, escalation contacts.
- Steward (rotation, 12–72h): watches guardrail dashboards, approves next step or reduces exposure.
- SRE / Ops: capacity and latency SLOs, circuit-break automation, rollback hooks.
- Solutions / Customer Eng: customer-specific risk assessments, opt-outs.
- Observability Engineer: signal instrumentation and runbook tests before smoke.

Pre-launch checklist (must be green before any external traffic):
- Metrics instrumented: per-slice latency p50/p95, cost-per-token, error-rate, hallucination-flag rate (from safety heuristics), business KPI (CTR, acceptance).
- Rollback automation: api route flag + traffic-slicing config, infra playbook tested in staging.
- Synthetic stress: run synthetic traffic profile matching peak QPS and sequence-length distribution.
- Stakeholder alignment: slack channel + escalation tree established, oncall aware of activation window.
- Audit trail: Confluence entry + JIRA ticket with hypothesis and expected metrics.

Safety & guardrail signals (primary)
- Latency breach: p95 > baseline_p95 * 1.5 or > absolute cap (e.g., 2s) for >5m.
- Error spike: 5xx or model runtime errors > 3x baseline rolling mean for 10m.
- Safety degradation: moderation flag rate or hallucination proxy > baseline + delta (set per-model).
- Business drop: primary KPI drop > relative threshold (e.g., CTR -5% absolute) with statistical significance.
- Cost runaway: cost-per-response > x2 expected for sustained 30m.
- Oscillation sentinel: repeated pass/fail cycles across slices (indicates sampling instability).

Decision heuristics for steward (fast rules):
- If any primary signal trips AND it persists for >10m, reduce exposure by 50% or revert to previous model variant.
- If latency/ops signal triggers but safety/business signals are clean, scale down slice sizes and enable human-review for affected slices.
- If business KPI shows degradation but safety/ops are normal, quarantine affected cohorts (geo/segment) and pause further ramp.
- If multiple weak signals across orthogonal metrics (latency+mod flags+cost) then immediate rollback to init-run is recommended.

A/B statistical quick-guides (for small runs)
- Use pragmatic thresholds: for early micro runs, focus on directional signals (consistent sign across two daily snapshots), avoid declaring significance.
- For ramp and broad: precompute sample size using baseline variance and minimum detectable effect (MDE). If expected daily active users per cohort < 3k, prefer repeated micro-runs instead of simple A/B.
- Avoid long, low-traffic experiments that drift; prefer iterative micro-experiments with guardrails.

Slice selection patterns (practical heuristics)
- Orthogonalize risk: choose slices that isolate capability differences (e.g., enterprise customers vs free users; long-context vs short-context).
- Prefer high-signal slices early: power users, edge-case queries, and logged-feedback cohorts. These surface quality changes faster.
- Keep reserved safety slices (human-review pool) that are always routed to the previous stable model for comparison.

Telemetry & dashboards (minimum panels)
- Exposure panel: slice, weight, variant, steward on duty, timestamp of last decision.
- Safety panel: moderation flags, hallucination proxies, human-review queue length.
- Ops panel: p50/p95 latency, QPS, infra errors, GPU utilization, queue depth.
- Business panel: engagement KPIs per slice, conversion rates, retention delta.
- Cost panel: cost per 1k tokens, e2e request cost, anomaly markers.

Communication templates (short)
- Activation notice (to slack channel): "Activating micro-run: feature X, variant B, slices: {A,B}, weight: 0.5%, steward: NAME, watch window: 6h. Links: <dashboards> <jira>."
- Alert escalation message: "Steward DECLARED: pause/revert recommended. Signal: LATENCY/SAFETY/CTR. Action taken: traffic reduced to X% / reverted to model vY. Details: <link>."

Post-activation cadence and artifacts
- Day 0–1: steward hourly checks first 6h, then 3x checks for next 18h. Rapid notes captured inline in the JIRA ticket.
- Day 2–7 (micro to ramp): daily steward summary with attachments (sample traces, failing prompts, top diff examples).
- Post-mortem: if rollback or notable degradation occurred, 72h post-incident writeup with root cause, mitigations, and safety net improvements.

Common failure patterns and mitigations
- Sampling contamination: variant leaks into control due to routing bug. Mitigate: replay logs, quarantine slice, freeze traffic until investigation.
- Regressions only on long-tail queries: increase sampling of long-context users and add targeted unit prompts to eval suite.
- Oscillation between slices (false positives from small counts): increase aggregation window or merge adjacent slices for stability.

Runbook snippets (copy-paste ops steps)
- Quick revert (CLI): rr rollback --route featureX --to stable --reason "safety spike"
- Pause traffic (console): open route > set weight 0 for variant B > apply > notify steward
- Emergency fallback: enable soft-fallback path that routes user to cached reply or prior model for 100% of requests for specific customer ID range

Lightweight experiment templates (starter hypotheses)
- Prompt-clarity micro: hypothesis: small prompt template reduces hallucination for long-context queries. Trellis: long-context slice, 0.2% weight. Success: hallucination proxy -30% within 48h, no latency penalty.
- Cost-trade micro: hypothesis: quantized variant reduces cost 30% with <2% metric drop. Trellis: enterprise + free slices, staggered weights. Success: cost-per-1k -30% sustained 24h, CTR delta within threshold.

Operational notes / open questions
- How strict should automatic rollback thresholds be for enterprise paid customers? (We need a policy matrix for contract-level exceptions.)
- Instrumentation gaps: hallucination proxy is noisy; need a second human-in-the-loop verification path for high-risk slices.
- Ownership: propose steward rota owned by product + solutions for first 90 days for any high-impact LLM feature.

Appendix: short glossary
- steward: short-shift operator responsible for active observation and decisions during exposure.
- slice: named cohort or request-routing filter used to partition traffic.
- trellis: 2D exposure matrix (slices x weights x variant metadata) used to stage rollout.
- oscillation: repeated toggling of exposure due to unstable signals.

Next steps (proposal)
- Pilot this cheatsheet with one upcoming micro-release (Feature: contextual-rerank Tweak). Assign steward rota and pre-flight checklist, run a 72h micro-run and capture run artifacts.
- Collect feedback and convert to a more formal runbook with step-by-step UI screenshots and CLI examples.

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep the cheatsheet intentionally short. Teams hate long playbooks during oncall.
- Build a small template in the Console: "start micro-run" that wires steward, dashboard links, and auto-notifications.

-- end of draft --
